text: Have you ever wondered where your bank keeps everyone's money?
If you think it's piled up in a vault under the building... you're wrong.
Yes, there's a vault. But it holds only a small part of the money.
Most of your money was never cash.
When you get paid by direct deposit, no bills move. The bank just changes a number.
That number is your deposit. And the bank doesn't let it sit still.
It lends it out. To a car buyer. A home buyer. A business.
Since twenty twenty, the legal minimum a U.S. bank must keep in reserve is zero percent.
Wait. Then what happens when you want your cash?
Banks keep some cash ready. When they need more, an armored truck brings it from the Federal Reserve.
And the bank's own reserves? Mostly numbers too, in an account at the Federal Reserve.
So the money isn't hiding under the bank. It's moving, as loans and as numbers.
And your deposit is insured up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars by the F.D.I.C.
So... did you think the money was in the vault? Yes or no, in the comments.
